Treatment summary
Treatment summary, prepared by the treating provider. The patient presented following a side-impact collision at an
intersection, with a wrist fracture that is consistent in type and mechanism with the force of that crash. Imaging and
examination findings clearly confirm the fracture. Over the course of care the patient attended forty visits, a volume
well above what is typical for this injury, with visits occurring almost daily for a period. Additional body regions were
reported and added to the treatment plan several weeks after the collision. Review of the outside records shows the
patient was under treatment for the same condition before the collision, and much of the current complaint appears to
stem from that earlier, ongoing problem rather than from the fracture alone. The billing records show no repeated or
duplicate charges for the same services. Recommendations are to continue orthopedic follow-up for the fracture,
reassess the remaining complaints once the prior condition is clarified, and coordinate with the patient's prior
providers.

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.
